problems.title: A difference-of-cubes graph
problems.question: Which listed point lies on $y=(1-x)(x^2+x+1)$?
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
steps: At x=2 the value is 1−8=−7, giving(2,−7). The other listed pairs fail substitution.

problems.title: Intersection coordinate product
problems.question: Find the coordinate product at the intersection of x+y=2 and 2x−y=−5.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: Add the equations to eliminate y: $3x=-3$.
steps: x=−1 and y=3. Multiply the coordinates.

problems.title: Y-intercept through two points
problems.question: A line passes through(−1,3) and(2,0). Find its y-intercept.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
steps: Its equation is y=−x+2, so x=0 gives y=2.

problems.title: When two circles share a point
problems.question: Circles have radii 7 and 2. Which listed centre distance is impossible if they share at least one point?
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The necessary and sufficient bounds are $|7-2|\le d\le7+2$, or $5\le d\le9$.
steps: Of5,6.2,8,7.5,9,4.5, only 4.5 lies outside these bounds.

problems.title: Check incompatible right-triangle radii
problems.question: A right triangle supposedly has inradius 7 and circumradius 13. Find the sum of its legs.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: For legs a, b and hypotenuse c, $c=2R=26$ and $r=(a+b-c)/2$, formally giving $a+b=40$.
steps: But a²+b²=c²=676 implies (a+b)²≤2(a²+b²)=1352, hence a+b≤26√2≈36.77. The formal value 40 is impossible. Equivalently every triangle satisfies R≥2r, contradicted by 13<14.
problems.answer: No such triangle exists. The formal listed sum is 40.
problems.note: The source radii are inconsistent. Using the radius formula alone yields 40, but no real pair of legs can have both that sum and hypotenuse 26.

problems.title: Read a linear function table
problems.question: A linear function has table x=0,2,−1 and f(x)=1,7,−2. Find its x-intercept.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
steps: Thus y=3x+1; the third table pair also satisfies it. Set y=0 to obtain x=−1/3.

problems.title: A remainder modulo eleven
problems.question: Find the remainder of 987654321 divided by 11.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: $10\equiv-1\pmod{11}$, so the alternating digit sum gives the same remainder.
steps: From the units digit,1−2+3−4+5−6+7−8+9=5. This already lies between 0 and 10.

problems.title: Quadrant after a coordinate change
problems.question: A=(x₁, y₁) lies in quadrant II. In which quadrant is B=(7−x₁,−y₁−13)?
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: Quadrant II means $x_1<0,y_1>0$.
steps: Thus 7−x₁>0 and −y₁−13<0. A positive x and negative y place B in quadrant IV.

problems.title: Angle between incentre lines
problems.question: O is the incentre of ABC and C=110°. Find the smaller angle between the lines AO and BO.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
steps: The smaller angle between the full lines is supplementary to 145°.

problems.title: Three arcs with ratio one to two to three
problems.question: Consecutive arcs MN, NK, KM have ratio 1:2:3, and chord MN+MK=9.6. Find the diameter.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The arcs are 60°,120°,180°. Thus MK is a diameter d and $MN=d\sin30°=d/2$.

problems.title: Perpendicular slope
problems.question: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line through(5,−4) and(−7,2).
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The original slope is $(2+4)/(-7-5)=-1/2$. Perpendicular slopes have product −1.

problems.title: A repeated modular root
problems.question: Natural a satisfies $a^2+20a+107\equiv0\pmod7$. Find the remainder of a.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: Modulo 7 the polynomial is $a^2-a+2$. Multiplying by 4 gives $(2a-1)^2\equiv0$.
steps: A prime dividing a square divides its base, so 2a−1≡0. The inverse of 2 modulo 7 is 4, giving a≡4.

problems.title: Parallel line through an intersection
problems.question: y=kx+b passes through the intersection of y=x−5 and y=−2x+1 and is parallel to 4x−y=1. Find b.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The intersection satisfies $x-5=-2x+1$, giving x=2, y=−3. The parallel slope is 4.
steps: Substitute−3=4·2+b.

problems.title: Angle of two tangents
problems.question: A chord divides a circle into arcs in ratio 4:11. Find the angle between its endpoint tangents.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The minor arc is $360°\cdot4/15=96°$. The angle between tangent rays from their intersection is 180° minus that arc.
steps: 180°−96°=84°. It is also the acute angle between the tangent lines.

problems.title: A diameter crossing an unequal chord
problems.question: A diameter meets a chord at A at 60°, splitting the chord into lengths 6 and 10. Find OA, where O is the circle centre.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The chord midpoint H satisfies $AH=(10-6)/2=2$ and $OH\perp AH$.
steps: Since OA lies on the diameter, the acute angle between OA and AH is 60°. In the right triangle OAH, AH=OAcos 60°=OA/2.

problems.title: Equidistant from two axes
problems.question: A=(2a+b,3b−a) is in quadrant IV and 7 from each coordinate axis. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The coordinates must be $(7,-7)$, so $2a+b=7$, $3b-a=-7$.
steps: From b=7−2a, the second equation gives 21−7a=−7, so a=4 and b=−1.

problems.title: Possible cancellation and digit sum
problems.question: For some natural n, $(n-13)/(3n+8)$ reduces by a natural factor m≠1. Which listed digit sum can m have?
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: Every common divisor divides $(3n+8)-3(n-13)=47$.
steps: 47 is prime, so the only possible m>1 is 47. It occurs at n=60, giving 47/188. The digit sum of 47 is 4+7.

problems.title: Quadrants a line must cross
problems.question: If y=kx+b has kb>0, which quadrants must it cross?
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: Either k, b are both positive or both negative.
steps: For k>0, b>0 the line crosses I, II, III. For k<0, b<0 it crosses II, III, IV. The common quadrants are II and III.

problems.title: Circumcentre angle versus incentre angle
problems.question: An acute triangle’s side AC subtends 140° at its circumcentre. What angle does it subtend at its incentre?
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The corresponding inscribed angle is B=140°/2=70°. The obtuse alternative 110° is excluded by acuteness.
steps: At the incentre, AIC=90°+B/2=90°+35°.

problems.title: Perimeter of a small tangent triangle
problems.question: ABC is a6–8–10 right triangle with AB=10, AC=8, BC=6. A tangent to its incircle cuts AB, AC internally at M, K. Find perimeter AMK.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: Equal tangent lengths from A to the incircle are $t=(AB+AC-BC)/2=6$.
steps: The incircle lies beyond MK relative to A. If its contact with MK splits that segment into lengths u, v, equality of tangents gives AM+u=t and AK+v=t. Therefore AM+AK+MK=(t−u)+(t−v)+(u+v)=2t.

problems.title: Compare two car speeds
problems.question: Cars from A, B meet after 5 hours. Increasing their speeds by 30%,15% makes the meeting time 4 hours. Compare their original speeds.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: For speeds u, v the same distance gives $5(u+v)=4(1.3u+1.15v)$.
steps: Expand:5u+5v=5.2u+4.6v, so .4v=.2u. Thus u=2v.
problems.answer: The car from A is twice as fast.

problems.title: Divisibility of three consecutive integers
problems.question: How many two-digit natural N satisfy $150\mid N^3-N$?
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: $N^3-N=N(N-1)(N+1)$ is always divisible by 6. Thus require divisibility by 25 as well. Among these consecutive factors, at most one is divisible by 5.
steps: Consequently that factor must be divisible by 25, giving N≡−1,0,1 mod 25. In10,…,99 these are 24,25,26,49,50,51,74,75,76,99.

problems.title: Integer pairs with a product bound
problems.question: Count integer pairs(x, y) satisfying 3x+5y=11 and |xy|≤15.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: All integer solutions are $x=2+5t,y=1-3t$, $t\in\mathbb Z$, giving $xy=2-t-15t^2$.
steps: For t=−1,0,1 the products are −12,2,−14, all valid. For t≥2 the absolute value is at least 60; for t≤−2 it is at least 56, and increases farther out. Thus only these three integers t work.

problems.title: Intersecting diagonals of an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: Chords AB, CD intersect at M, arcs AC and BD are equal, AMD=120°, MC=6, and M is 8 from chord AD. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: Equal arcs give equal inscribed angles, implying $AD\parallel BC$. Equal opposite arcs also give the isosceles symmetry, so $AM=DM$ and $BM=CM$.
steps: Thus BM=6. In isosceles triangle AMD the altitude to AD bisects angle M=120°, making a right triangle with angle 60° at M. Hence 8=AMcos 60°=AM/2, so AM=16. Add AM+MB.

problems.title: Tangent circles and an exterior bisector
problems.question: Two unequal circles touch externally at A. A tangent at B on the smaller circle crosses the larger circle at C, D, with C between B, D. If CAB=68°, find CAD.
problems.idea: Use the graph, equation, or circle relation and check the original conditions.
formulas: The negative homothety centred at A taking the small circle to the large one sends B to E on the opposite ray from AB. The tangent at E is parallel to CD.
steps: A chord parallel to the tangent at E has equal arcs from E to its two endpoints C, D. Thus the line AE, also AB, bisects an exterior angle between AC and AD at A. Since B is outside the larger circle and C, D lie on the same ray from B, this is the exterior-angle bisector configuration. Therefore CAB=(180°−CAD)/2.
Set 68°=(180°−CAD)/2 and solve.
